note: Hard exclusion gates. A definitive negative result for a specific marker outranks any number of non-specific secondary signals, and suppresses the condition outright rather than merely lowering its score. Evaluated before cohort confidence and before disease scoring.
principles: Only an EXPLICIT definitive negative activates a gate. A missing test never does - missing stays unknown and is handled by coverage, not by veto.
An equivocal or indeterminate result never activates a gate.
A positive result never activates a gate; the normal rules then evaluate as usual.
A gate suppresses the condition, any cohort listed, and any recommendation derived from them. The reason is recorded for audit.

rules.user_message: A negative HBsAg rules this out, so it is not reported even though other liver markers are abnormal.
rules.basis: HBsAg is the defining surface-antigen marker for Hepatitis B. The Disease Master row for Hepatitis B names 'Positive HBsAg with elevated liver enzymes' as its High-Risk Indicator, so an explicitly negative HBsAg removes the defining half of that criterion. Raised ALT/AST/lymphocytes are non-specific and must not substitute for it.
rules.threshold_source: The 0.90 COI cut-off was supplied by the project owner. It is NOT derived from the Disease Master, which contains no numeric thresholds.

rules.user_message: A negative Anti-HCV rules this out, so it is not reported even though other liver markers are abnormal.
rules.basis: Disease Master High-Risk Indicators for Hepatitis C: 'Positive Anti-HCV with elevated liver enzymes'. An explicit negative removes the defining half of that criterion.
rules.threshold_source: Status-only rule. No numeric cut-off is configured because none was supplied; add 'numeric_below' here if the assay's COI cut-off is known.

rules.user_message: A negative Hepatitis A IgM rules out acute infection, so it is not reported even though other liver markers are abnormal.
rules.basis: Disease Master High-Risk Indicators for Hepatitis A: 'Markedly elevated SGOT/SGPT with jaundice and positive Anti-HAV IgM'. An explicit negative IgM removes the acute-infection criterion.
rules.threshold_source: Status-only rule; no numeric cut-off supplied.

rules.user_message: A non-reactive HIV screen rules this out, so it is not reported even though immune markers are abnormal.
rules.basis: Disease Master High-Risk Indicators for HIV: 'Reactive HIV screening test confirmed by a second confirmatory method'. A non-reactive screen removes that criterion. The Immune Status Monitoring row applies only to 'a confirmed HIV-positive individual' by its own wording.
rules.threshold_source: Status-only rule; no numeric cut-off supplied.

rules.user_message: A non-reactive VDRL/RPR rules this out, so it is not reported.
rules.basis: Disease Master High-Risk Indicators for Syphilis: 'Reactive VDRL/RPR confirmed by treponemal test'. A non-reactive screen removes that criterion.
rules.threshold_source: Status-only rule; no numeric cut-off supplied.

rules.reason: Dengue NS1 and IgM both explicitly negative
rules.user_message: Negative dengue NS1 and IgM rule this out, so it is not reported even though platelets are low.
rules.basis: Disease Master High-Risk Indicators for Dengue Fever: 'Positive NS1/IgM with falling platelet count and rising hematocrit'. With BOTH serological arms explicitly negative, a low platelet count alone must not raise dengue. 'also_negative' requires every listed marker to be explicitly negative before the gate activates, so a negative NS1 with IgM missing does NOT veto.
rules.threshold_source: Status-only rule; no numeric cut-off supplied.

rules.user_message: A negative malaria test rules this out, so it is not reported.
rules.basis: Disease Master High-Risk Indicators for Malaria: 'Positive blood smear/antigen test'. An explicit negative removes that criterion.
rules.threshold_source: Status-only rule; no numeric cut-off supplied.

not_implemented.candidate: Numeric COI cut-offs for Anti-HCV, Anti-HAV IgM, HIV, VDRL, dengue and malaria assays
not_implemented.why: Only the HBsAg cut-off (0.90 COI) was supplied. Assay cut-offs vary by manufacturer and the Disease Master carries no numeric thresholds, so inventing them would be unsafe. Each rule above already accepts a 'numeric_below' key - add the value when the assay is known and it takes effect with no code change.
